grammarPoint.title: Future perfect
grammarPoint.summary: Use the future perfect to talk about actions that will be completed before a specific time or event in the future.
grammarPoint.explanation:
The future perfect tense describes an action that will be finished *before* a certain point in the future. It emphasizes the completion of an action by a future deadline or event.

We often use time expressions like *by*, *by the time*, *before*, or *in X years/months* with the future perfect to indicate the future completion point.

Think of it as looking back from a future moment and seeing that an action has already happened. It's not about when the action starts, but when it will be done.
patterns: Subject + will not have + past participle (won't have)

examples.text: By 2025, they will have built the new bridge.
examples.note: The building will be completed before the year 2025.

examples.text: I won't have finished my report by the time you get home.
examples.note: The report will still be incomplete when you arrive.

examples.text: Will you have eaten dinner before the movie starts?
examples.note: Asking if the action of eating will be completed before a future event.

examples.text: She will have lived in Paris for five years next month.
examples.note: The action of living will reach a five-year duration by next month.

examples.text: The team will have practiced for hours by the end of the day.
examples.note: The practice will be completed, lasting for hours, by the day's end.

commonErrors.wrong: By next week, I will finish the project.
commonErrors.right: By next week, I *will have finished* the project.
commonErrors.note: Use future perfect to show completion by a future time.

commonErrors.wrong: They will have went to the store already.
commonErrors.right: They *will have gone* to the store already.
commonErrors.note: Always use the past participle form of the main verb.

commonErrors.wrong: She has have completed her work by then.
commonErrors.right: She *will have completed* her work by then.
commonErrors.note: The auxiliary verb for future perfect is 'will have', not 'has have'.

exercises.question: By the time we arrive, the concert ___.
exercises.explanation: The concert will be completed (started) before our arrival, so the future perfect is correct.

exercises.question: How many books ___ by the end of the year?
exercises.explanation: The question asks about the completion of reading books by a future point, requiring the future perfect.

exercises.question: I'm sure they ___ the new software by Monday.
exercises.explanation: The action of installing will be completed before Monday, so 'will have installed' is correct.

exercises.question: Don't worry, I ___ the dishes before you wake up.
exercises.explanation: The action of washing the dishes will be completed before the future event of you waking up.

exercises.text: By next month, I ___ ___ (save) enough money for my trip.
exercises.explanation: The action of saving will be completed by next month, so 'will have saved' is the correct future perfect form.

exercises.text: She ___ ___ (not finish) her presentation before the deadline.
exercises.explanation: The negative future perfect 'will not have finished' (or 'won't have finished') indicates the presentation will still be incomplete by the deadline.

exercises.text: ___ they ___ (arrive) at the airport by 3 PM?
exercises.explanation: This is a question asking about the completion of arrival by a future time, so 'Will they have arrived' is correct.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: The sentence uses the future perfect to show that the action of moving will be completed by next year.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.explanation: This sentence uses the negative future perfect to indicate that the action of seeing the movie will not be completed by tonight.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: By the time you call, I will eat lunch.
answers: By the time you call, I will have eaten lunch.
exercises.explanation: The action of eating lunch will be completed before the future event of you calling, so the future perfect 'will have eaten' is needed.

exercises.prompt: Find the mistake and write the sentence correctly.
exercises.sentence: They will have finish the report before Friday.
answers: They will have finished the report before Friday.
exercises.explanation: The future perfect requires the past participle form of the main verb, which is 'finished', not 'finish'.

exercises.source: I will complete my studies in two years.
answers: By 2026, I will have completed my studies.
exercises.explanation: The instruction requires expressing completion by a future date, which is the function of the future perfect.

exercises.source: The guests will arrive before 8 PM.
exercises.instruction: Rewrite to emphasize the completion of their arrival by 8 PM.
answers: The guests will have arrived by 8 PM.
By 8 PM, the guests will have arrived.
exercises.explanation: Changing to the future perfect 'will have arrived' emphasizes that the action of arriving will be completed before the specified future time.

extra.question: By 2030, scientists ___ a cure for many common diseases.
extra.explanation: The discovery will be completed before 2030.

extra.question: She ___ her degree by next summer.
extra.explanation: The action of getting her degree will be completed before next summer.

extra.question: ___ you ___ your presentation slides before the meeting starts?
extra.explanation: Asking if the preparation will be completed before the meeting.

extra.question: I can't meet you at 5 PM. By then, I ___ work for the day.
extra.explanation: The action of finishing work will be completed before 5 PM.
